The film follows two siblings who are close they “speak in unison, love the same man, and have the same dreams,” according to the synopsis. It was directed by Werner Herzog, the influential German filmmaker of “Nosferatu the Vampyre” and “Aguirre, Wrath of God.” Related Stories Meghan Markle’s ‘The Gentlemen’ Rumors May Have Overshadowed Season 2 Launch — but Her Role Isn’t Off the Table Shonda Rhimes Renews Netflix Overall Deal for Another Five Years “At first, it was very daunting, the idea that we were going to be playing this kind of same person,” Rooney said at a Venice Film Festival press conference ahead of the movie’s premiere on Thursday. “But I think we found pretty quickly that having a lifetime together and all this history and a childhood of playing together. There was just an unspoken world between us that we didn’t have to work very hard to create at all. I’ve never laughed so much, it was a very once in a lifetime, unique experience.” Popular on Variety Kate added that speaking in synchronicity “felt almost like a song.” “We had this unspoken sort of rhythm together,” she said. “It was very musical. The filmmaker added that the sisters “hardly needed any rehearsals” to get the speaking right. Though they had two weeks of alotted prep time time, Herzog was ready to roll the cameras after just five days. “I had complete confidence with them,” he said. “Bucking Fastard” is loosely inspired by real British identical twins Freda and Greta Chaplin, who became tabloid sensations after becoming besotted with their neighbor, who eventually took out a restraining order on them. The movie’s daring title comes from a spoonerism the twins made (simultaneously, of course) while they were in court. Orlando Bloom and Domhnall Gleeson round out the cast. title: USA Sports Will Serve Up World Team Tennis Reboot (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All September 3, 2026 5:00am Jessica Pegula Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images World Team Tennis has found a media partner for its revival, after a five year hiatus. The mixed gender tennis league that was co-founded by Billie Jean King in 1974 has inked a deal with USA Sports to televise WTT matches, with all six games running in primetime on CNBC , and streaming on Fandango. WTT and Versant will also partner on other integrations via E! and some of the media company’s other properties. Matches will begin Dec. 1 and run through Dec. 15, keeping the matches outside of the Grand Slam tennis calendar. WTT last held a season in November 2021, before pandemic-spurred challenges forced the hiatus. The league announced its reboot plans earlier this year, including giving athletes equity in the league. Jessica Pegula, Tommy Paul and Denis Shapovalov are among the players committed. The league has long relied on city-based teams, and the new version of WTT will follow that model with the New York Empire Racquet Club, based at Barclays Center; Toronto North Racquet Club based at Coca-Cola Coliseum; and Florida Flamingos Racquet Club at Amerant Bank Arena. It will also have a new format, with four singles sets and a mixed doubles tiebreaker. The league also plans to utilize immersive technology, live music, and other elements to enhance the in-person and televised experiences. “In creating a new era of World Team Tennis, our goal is to build a sports and entertainment property that delivers value to fans wherever they are, while tapping into adjacent audiences that can help grow the sport,” said WTT CEO Stephen Amritraj. “Versant’s portfolio is uniquely compelling because it allows us to do both. CNBC has a natural connection to the traditional tennis audience while Fandango provides an opportunity to reach fans from a streaming perspective.” USA Sports has been opportunistic in snagging new sports rights, supplementing its core WNBA, NASCAR, PGA Tour and international soccer with a heavy emphasis on deals it sees as growth opportunities. That includes League One Volleyball and the Pro Padel League. While the flagship sports are running on USA Network, parent company Versant has also begun to use CNBC (which is also about as widely distributed as cable channels can get) for some sports, and turning Fandango into a streaming destination. “We’re excited to bring live World Team Tennis to CNBC and Fandango this December,” said Celia Kohl, SVP of Strategy & Business Development at Versant. “USA Sports is always looking to bring growth-minded leagues that innovate and excite into our portfolio, and we believe WTT is one of those leagues that will resonate with our audiences across both CNBC and Fandango.” THR

title: ‘Everest: The Other Side’ Review: A Frustrating, Guiltily Compelling Portrait of the Triumph and Tragedy of Extreme Mountaineering
full_text: × Skip to main content By Richard Lawson Plus Icon Richard Lawson View All September 3, 2026 5:00am 'Everest: The Other Side' Photo: Jimmy Chin In their gripping, Oscar-winning 2018 documentary Free Solo , husband and wife directors Jimmy Chin and Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi examine the boggling daring of Alex Honnold, a rock climber who scales sheer mountain walls without the aid, and protection, of ropes. The film’s climbing scenes are breathtakingly tense, but what sells the movie as more than mere docu-thriller is its sharp assessment of Honnold’s psychological makeup, the jumble of genetics and conditioning that have turned him into a man seemingly unaffected by fear. He’s oddly charming in all his insouciant disregard for his own safety, but there’s something sinister there, too. He takes on these feats with only a small amount of concern for how an accident might impact those who love him, including the woman to whom he’s now married. Honnold is free to not care about himself, but shouldn’t he more thoroughly consider the emotions of those around him? That said, those people are all adults with their own agency; they could choose, much as it might hurt, to walk away from Honnold whenever they pleased. Had children been in the picture, though, Honnold’s death-defying acts would be unforgivable. Related Stories Movies Martin McDonagh Discusses His CIA Drama 'Wild Horse Nine,' Set in a Time When "Horrible People Had Intelligence" Movies 'Eklipse' Mixes the Autobiographical and Fictional to Explore AIDS Taboos and Fear of Social Exclusion Everest: The Other Side The Bottom Line An accidental rebuttal to George Mallory’s ‘Because it’s there.’ Venue : Venice Film Festival (Venice Open — Out of Competition) Directors: Jimmy Chin, Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi 1 hour 55 minutes And thus the central — and enormous — problem with Chin and Vasarhelyi’s new film, Everest: The Other Side , a portrait of two reckless, ruthlessly self-involved people who like to climb very tall mountains and then ski down them. The documentary begins with couple Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson preparing to do something unprecedented: They will scale Mt. Everest’s notoriously difficult north face (the part on the China side of the mountain) and then strap on their skis and head back the way they came. Why they want to do this is explained in the typical grandiose, solipsistic terms. It is a craving for extreme experience that, in Morrison’s and Nelson’s (and the film’s) minds, better connects them to themselves and to the universe. This is more than a passion, they insist. It is a primal need that cannot be denied. “Okay,” we think, watching these two gas each other up. “But what about Nelson’s sons?” Y’know, the two living, breathing, helpless children forced to sit idle while their mother and (almost) step-father constantly and brazenly risk abandoning them. All of the big talk about personal drive, which makes Free Solo so darkly compelling, immediately crumbles into selfish pablum the second that children are introduced into the equation. Rather than heroic, these costly and horribly uncertain stunts come across callous and cruel. Hideous proof of that arrives 20 or so minutes into The Other Side , when we see Nelson in the final seconds before she fell to her death while attempting to ski down the world’s eighth-tallest mountain. One moment she is on her skis testing her position, and in the next the shelf of snow beneath her dislodges and slides off a nearly 6,000-foot cliff. In an awful instant, two boys lose their mother and the movie loses any kind of principled posture. A more inquisitive film might have then turned its gaze inward, becoming a meta investigation of what all this thrill-seeking has wrought, a study of hubris and hamartia. Instead, The Other Side shifts into triumph-over-grief mode, as Morrison prepares to fulfill the Everest mission in honor of his late partner. We learn more about Morrison’s backstory, particularly a baroquely terrible tragedy he endured 15 years ago. It’s impossible to not feel immense pity for Morrison, who suffered something unimaginable. But that sympathy can’t quite make up for the galling fact of Nelson’s sons, now teenagers stuck in limbo as a father figure stubbornly insists on courting further ruin. What’s even more shocking is that Chin, himself a mountaineer, decides to embark on the Everest trip with Morrison (and a load of other men), though he has young children of his own at home. Vasarhelyi appears on camera, wondering where the end of this might be. She asks Chin how many people who have sat at their dinner table are now dead, and in response Chin calmly rattles off a staggeringly long list of names. Are we nonetheless supposed to root for Chin’s decision to support his friend? The Other Side answers an indignant “yes.” What ensues is, in a purely visceral way, wholly transfixing. Extreme mountain climbing has never looked anything but miserable from the distance of a screening room, and The Other Side delivers mightily on all that scraping, straining, gasping toil. While it may only offer limp gestures of acknowledgment to the underpaid and dangerous labor of the Sherpas who facilitate the adventures of well-funded Western men (and a few women), the film still envelops us in the intense rigor and fortitude of Morrison’s pursuit. Its images are stunning, in both exacting close-up and wide, sweeping drone shots. A palpable suspense overtakes us as Morrison and his team work their way up this daunting monolith, potential cataclysm lurking in every crack of rock and tumble of snow. Cynically or not, Chin and Vasarhelyi understand that these primal thrills are enough to distract us from the frustrating and sorrowful truth at the center of the story. Well, almost enough. Every time the film cuts back to Nelson’s sons, we are reminded that none of this needs to happen, that a lot of people would still be alive today had they only ignored the juvenile, daredevil id they have dressed up as noble calling. The Other Side works hard to combat or paste over the heavy moral questions it provokes, uplifting ending and all. But I left the theater feeling angry and bitter, suddenly put off by the whole project of mountaineering. Senseless death (or risk of death) is simply not inspiring, no matter what jockish bromides Morrison, Nelson, Chin, et al. throw at us. Basely captivated as I was by the mighty struggle up The Other Side , my mind kept drifting back to that dinner table, to Vasarhelyi’s anguished bewilderment that her husband has decided to put his children in danger of losing a parent in order to honor a colleague who did indeed inflict that dreadful fate on her own children. If only the film had lingered longer on Vasarhelyi’s totally rational horror and disbelief. But I guess that wouldn’t make for a very exciting mountain-climbing documentary, would it? Full credits Venue: Venice Film Festival (Venice Open — Out of Competition) Production companies: National Geographic Documentary Films, Little Monster Films Directors: Jimmy Chin, Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi Cinematograpy: Clair Popkin, Jimmy Chin, Christopher Murphy Editing: Bob Eisenhardt, Simona Ferrari Music: Caroline Ho 1 hour 55 minutes THR

title: Gloria Steinem Dies: Feminist Icon And Activist & Co-Founder Of Ms. Magazine Was 92
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Gloria Steinem Dies: Feminist Icon And Activist & Co-Founder Of Ms. Magazine Was 92 Tubi Turns To Football Freestylers Woody & Kleiny For First UK Original From Creators Program Goalhanger Wants To Make The “British Bourne” With Geopolitical Audio Drama ‘Bear Hunt’ View All September 3, 2026 4:27am Gloria Steinem in 1972 Chuck Fishman/Getty Images Gloria Steinem , the American feminist icon and founder of Ms. magazine, died Wednesday, September 2, at her home in New York City. She was 92. Her death was announced in a joint post on her Instagram account and The Gloria Steinem Foundation. A cause of death was not disclosed, but the statement said she “passed passed away peacefully at her home in New York City, surrounded by some of the many who loved her.” “Gloria’s greatest gift was her ability to listen to others, to make others feel seen and heard. Her words, actions, and example gave people permission to be their truest selves,” the post read. “Gloria lived true to her independent spirit, always with curiosity and a great sense of humor.” Read the full note below. Related Stories News Jean-Paul Rappeneau Dies: 'Cyrano de Bergerac' Director Was 94 News Donald Trump Pays Tribute To Dolly Parton, Says He's Lowering U.S. Flags To Honor Entertainer In becoming one of the most-listened to voices in U.S. feminism, Steinem had spent most of her career in journalism. Among her most notable early stories was an exposé on Hugh Hefner’s Playboy empire, during which she went undercover as a Playboy Bunny to uncover the conditions facing the young women. Watch on Deadline The story caused a huge debate in American society, though Steinem later said she regretted the assignment as the association blighted the rest of her career. She went on to become a founder of Ms., which was among the first magazines to address women as more than housewives and homemakers in America. Steinem also was an early supporter of Women’s Action Alliance, a group focused on combating sexism. During the 1970s, she became a key advocate for abortion rights after being inspired by women speaking at Roe vs Wade case, where the Supreme Court made abortion a constitutional right. The right was repealed in 2022, prompting Steinem to write in an email to the AP, “Either our control over our own bodies is equal, regardless of sex or race, or we’re not living in a democracy. A documentary about Steinem’s life, Gloria: In Her Own Words , launched in 2011. Her memoir, My Life on the Road , was the basis for Julie Taymor biopic The Glorias , and she appeared on screen on the likes of 60 Minutes , The Daily Show and Charlie Rose and even in scripted series The Good Wife and And Just Like That… as herself. title: ‘The Girl With The Leica’ Review: Love Is War In Alina Marazzi’s Unconventional Biopic Of A Pioneering War Photographer – Venice Film Festival
full_text: Skip to main content By Damon Wise Damon Wise Film Editor, Awards yo_damo More Stories By Damon ‘The Girl With The Leica’ Review: Love Is War In Alina Marazzi’s Unconventional Biopic Of A Pioneering War Photographer – Venice Film Festival Venice Film Festival 2026: Read All Of Deadline’s Reviews Kenneth Branagh On Moving From Shakespeare To Action-Comedy In ‘Mayday’: “I Thought Zach Galifianakis Should Play The Part, But I Was Very Pleased They Asked Me” – Edinburgh Film Festival View All September 3, 2026 4:07am ‘The Girl With The Leica’ Manuel Alberto Claro The Venice Film Festival opened this week with Danny Boyle’s Ink , which, while not strictly a documentary, deals with fundamental issues of truth in news reporting — is the news we consume always true, and is the truth necessarily always news? Alina Marazzi’s The Girl With The Leica , a jazzed-up, unconventional biopic of the late photojournalist Gerda Taro — who died while covering the Spanish Civil at the age of 26 — poses a slightly more specific question about war reporting, in particular the fine line between bravery and ego in the process of bringing back dispatches from the front line. In that sense, there’s quite a lot of crossover with Ellen Kuras’s 2023 film Lee , which starred Kate Winslet as World War Two photojournalist Lee Miller, and while Marazzi has done her best to make her film stylistically different, the similarities will likely make it harder for her film to find an audience. Add to that the constant but often confusing zipping around between countries and time periods — the film only really covers five years in Taro’s life — and a trio of men kept dangling on string (Taro literally suggests in voiceover that her private life was also a battlefield) and you have a film that over-complicates a simple yet quite profound meditation on an artist’s identity and legacy. Related Stories Festivals Calls Grow For Palestinian Flag To Fly At Venice Film Festival As Artistic Director Says Not Possible To Meet Request News 'Ink': What The Critics Are Saying About Danny Boyle's Origin Story Of Brit Tabloid The Sun The film starts in Paris but Taro’s story begins in her native Leipzig in 1932, where Gerta Pohorylle, as she is then known, is a young woman whose political conscience is awakened by the rise of fascism. Taro (Emilia Schüle) dances to manic jazz and attends rousing left-wing sermons in nicotine-stained coffee bars, plastering the streets with illegal anti-Nazi posters. The pressure is becoming too much to bear, and one by one her circle of friends decamp to the only slightly safer environs of pre-war Paris. The Leipzig scenes are both ephemeral and integral; later, Taro will speculate that if the Germans had had the same revolutionary zeal as the Spanish, Hitler might have been defeated. Watch on Deadline In Paris, after living in near-poverty with her best friend Ruth, she meets Endre Friedmann (Aaron Altaras), a Hungarian photographer who takes Taro on as his assistant and eventually his protégé. It is Taro that devises a whole new identity not just for herself (as Taro) but for Friedmann, who is henceforth to be known as Robert Capa, a mysterious American playboy figure with Italian roots. Together, Taro and Capa blaze a trail in war reporting, documenting the Spanish Civil War with photographs depicting the ordinary the men and women who are fighting, the latter inspiring Taro to adopt the blue jumpsuit that became her signature. Capa and Taro worked as one, with Capa taking most of the credit, but the film doesn’t seem very interested in that. Taro is not in it for the glory, she sees her job as “taking part in history”, but the inherent sexism of the wider world does not pass her by (“To photograph means I exist,” she muses, “but the world only sees Capa”). The duo’s work features heavily throughout, and Marazzi leans heavily on archive footage, even weaving in sections of then-contemporary avant-garde films such as the Bertolt Brecht-scripted Kuhle Wampe , Jean Vigo’s L’Atalante and Joris Ivans’ The Spanish Earth , narrated by Ernest Hemingway. Hemingway is a useful touchstone, it transpires, reflected Taro’s growing — and increasingly romantic — obsession with the Spanish cause. There are, inevitably, lots of conversations about photography, “the instant of the gaze”, and “the miracle of the Leica”, which, due to its compact size, allowed Capa and Taro to work almost unnoticed in the middle of a warzone. More satisfying, though, is the film’s sense of irony about photography as an artform: though a great photograph can endure, it can just as easily be lost to history, as, indeed, was a significant chunk of Taro’s work. Nothing illustrates this better than a scene in which Capa finds out that the love of his life is dead, killed by a tank, and he realizes to his horror that he only has two pictures of the two of them together. In that single moment, all pretension flies out of the window and we see photography in its purest, most human form: the need to hold on to a moment. title: Amelia Dimoldenberg’s Hit YouTube Series ‘Chicken Shop Date’ To End After 12-Year Run
full_text: Skip to main content By Diana Lodderhose Diana Lodderhose International Features Editor @dianalodderhose More Stories By Diana ‘Art Sex Music’: First Look At Caroline Catz’s Doc About British Artist & Musician Cosey Fanni Tutti ‘Bunker’: Watch Javier Bardem & Penélope Cruz In Florian Zeller’s Venice-Bound Psychological Thriller Cynthia Erivo, Andrew Scott, Ava DuVernay, Jesse Eisenberg & More Set For London Film Festival Screen Talks Program View All September 3, 2026 3:49am Amelia Dimoldenberg Dimz Inc. Amelia Dimoldenberg , the creator behind Chicken Shop Date , has announced that she is bringing the hit YouTube interview series to a close after a “final few dates”. The online creator, who began the series as a column at the age of 17 and has since interviewed talent such as Billie Eilish, Andrew Garfield and Paul McCartney, made the announcement on Thursday on her Instagram account. “When I was 17, I thought that I might meet the love of my life on a date in a chicken shop,” she said. “Since then, I’ve spent my entire twenties sat across from the most incredible people, people I’d always dreamt of meeting. All of them charmed me (some more than others), and I definitely charmed them. Related Stories News 'Chicken Shop Date' Star Amelia Dimoldenberg Developing 'Skins'-Style Drama For The BBC Festivals Edinburgh Television Festival Advisory Chair Adam Hawkins Urges Industry To "Embrace Change" In Confab's Final Year In Scotland “To me, the show is my very own romcom, and I have loved being able to share it with you. I am so grateful to everyone who has followed me on this journey and found a bit of joy in these episodes. I never thought I’d end Chicken Shop Date . I thought maybe it would be a part of my life forever, and in some way it always will, but I feel like it’s now time to move on from this adventure and onto the next one.” Watch on Deadline Chicken Shop Date sees Dimoldenberg ask guests a series of questions in a flirty, and often awkward way, while on a date in a fried chicken restaurant. While the brand initially started off as a column in a youth-run magazine, Dimoldenberg parlayed the idea into a digital series which has been increasingly used by film marketing teams as part of the press cycle for film promotion. In recent years, the show, which Dimoldenberg has been producing under her Dimz Inc. label, has attracted top tier actors such as Garfield, Cynthia Erivo, Idris Elba as well as Paul Mescal, Harris Dickenson, Louis Theroux and Jack Harlow. Dimoldenberg’s YouTube channel has more than 3.4 million subscribers. Since 2022, the series’ social following increased from 830,000 to 4.4 million and on YouTube, the series has driven around one billion views across its run. According to a statement, the final Chicken Shop Date series will have “a last line-up of eclectic guests joining Amelia in the chicken shop before she closes this chapter.” Last week, at the Edinburgh TV Festival, Dimoldenberg said that she is developing a young adult drama series for the BBC, which she dubbed as “my version of Skins .” She is also developing an upcoming romantic comedy film with Amazon MGM Studios’ Orion Pictures. ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Rides Into Awards Race; Mohsen Gharaei; Palestine Call Jeff Goldblum To Host S2 Premiere Of ‘Saturday Night Live UK’ Unifrance Rendez-Vous TV Preview & Interview Amid Industry Shifts Scroll Through Photos From Opening Day Of The 83rd Venice Film Festival Read More About: Comments

title: French TV In Focus: Screenings & Shows To Watch At The Unifrance Rendez-Vous
full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart Unifrance’s Rendez-Vous Brings French Sellers & Global Buyers Together Amid Industry Shifts VodafoneThree Launching Vodafone TV In The UK, Bundling Netflix, HBO Max & Live Channels ‘Miraculous’ Studio Founder Jeremy Zag To Receive Deadline’s French TV Disruptor Award At The Unifrance Rendez-Vous View All September 3, 2026 3:49am Screenings at the Unifrance Rendez-Vous Jeremy Charbaut, Unifrance The Unifrance Rendez-Vous is about to get underway, with the French distributors presenting their wares to international buyers. The focus is squarely on French programming and buyers are getting a look at the best Gallic fare ahead of the trip to MIPCOM a month later. Despite being a sizable market, the Rendez-Vous is a fairly intimate affair, as acquisition and sales execs mingle on the main floor, but also at receptions, screenings and drinks. Here’s a run-down of the big screenings and big-ticket shows coming to the Rendez-Vous. Related Stories News Unifrance's Rendez-Vous Brings French Sellers & Global Buyers Together Amid Industry Shifts News 'Miraculous' Studio Founder Jeremy Zag To Receive Deadline's French TV Disruptor Award At The Unifrance Rendez-Vous Screenings: Big Beasts & Period Drama Watch on Deadline The first of a trio of official screenings at the Rendez-Vous is Beasts of the Colosseum , with Balanga across international sales. The one-off doc uses AI to tell the story of how Rome hosted wild spectacles for its citizens, featuring a range of exotic and dangerous wild animals. Next up in the screenings roster is Swapped , a six-part period drama from France TV Distribution. Set in Paris in 1899, it tells the story of Rose, who goes into service for a wealthy family and has to take extreme measures to keep her child. Completing the official screenings is another period piece, The Red and the Black , which is being distributed by Wild Bunch . An adaptation of the Stendhal novel, it follows Julien Sorel, a brilliant young man, torn between his fierce ambition and true love. Cozy Crime & Drama The Unifrance Rendez-Vous is a market for all types of show and as such spans everything from docs to animation to drama. With France established as a producer and distributor of cozy crime – a genre much in vogue with buyers, who appreciate its wide appeal and flexibility in schedules – there are several new shows to look out for. About Premium Content has Country Spy , a light crime series about Marie-Line Maupain, a spy for the French secret service who is abruptly frozen out by her superiors and sent back to her home town. The Deal Gaumont In terms of straight drama, Gaumont is in town with its Series Mania winner The Deal , which goes inside high-level nuclear weapons talks. In somewhat similar waters, SND will be selling R91 , its drama series about a murder on a nuclear aircraft carrier. Studio TF1 shows up at Le Havre with Season 2 of its crime drama Carpe Diem . Docs On The Dock There is always a strong line up of documentaries at the Rendez-Vous, with sellers turning up at the waterfront location with new factual shows. Andana Films heads to Le Havre with Gaza, a People’s History , which explores the history of Gaza with historians, experts, residents and witnesses of various conflicts that have beset the territory. Arte Distribution has Origins, A Tale of Light , a science doc that uses images created by artist Roman Hill, about the origins of the Universe. Blending animation and factual, Java Films is shopping A Night in the Channel , an animated film that reconstructs the harrowing moments when a dinghy carrying would-be immigrants sinks in the Channel. Toon Highlights Submarine Jim CBBC France has a rich history of animation and kids programming. At the Unifrance Rendez-Vous, Mediawan Kids & Family will have Witch Detectives , about three best friends who are also trainee witches. Millimages will be in town with Calypso . Its heroine, Calypso, wakes up each day to find her dreams – or nightmares – become part of her real life. Oggy and the Cockroaches outfit Xilam, meanwhile, has Submarine Jim , about a naive young dolphin who takes charge of a submarine that has charted a course for Las Vegas. The Unifrance Rendez-Vous runs from September 7 to 10 in Le Havre. title: Tubi Turns To Football Freestylers Woody & Kleiny For First UK Original From Creators Program
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Gloria Steinem Dies: Feminist Icon And Activist & Co-Founder Of Ms. Magazine Was 92 Tubi Turns To Football Freestylers Woody & Kleiny For First UK Original From Creators Program Goalhanger Wants To Make The “British Bourne” With Geopolitical Audio Drama ‘Bear Hunt’ View All September 3, 2026 3:30am 'Wheel of Misfortune' Tubi EXCLUSIVE: Tubi has put its boots on for a first UK original made with creators. The free streaming platform has ordered Wheel of Misfortune , a series from football freestylers Paul Wood and Paul Klein, or Woody & Kleiny, who have nearly 16 million YouTube followers and over five million on Instagram. The show will see the pair, who have previously showcased their skills on Britain’s Got Talent , spinning a wheel and doing “hilarious, brutal or downright ridiculous” forfeits. “Who will survive the chaos and who will regret spinning?,” asks the synopsis. Related Stories News Tubi Adds 'Once Upon A Time In Hollywood,' 'Jurassic World' & More To International Service With Sony & NBCU Deals News Wall Of Entertainment Partners With AI Platform Chronicle Media To Boost 'Substitute Teacher' & 'House Rules' On YouTube The commission comes through the Tubi for Creators initiative, which first launched in the U.S. last year to showcase more than 500 episodes from the likes of FunnyMike, Watcher and Jubilee. Watch on Deadline Tubi says one in six Tubi UK viewers watched creator content in July, accounting for more than 10% of total watch time in the country. The streamer offers more than 25,000 episodes from more than 400 creators, and launched its Creatorverse Hub last month across its markets. According to a YouGov poll from 2025, adult-age Gen Zs and Millennials made up 51% of Tubi’s UK audience. Wheel of Misfortune marks Woody & Kleiny’s first TV commission, with their content to date having been self-published. “Creators have built some of today’s most passionate fandoms, and Woody & Kleiny have proven that they don’t need to become anything other than who they are to make great entertainment,” said Sami Qasem, Tubi’s Director of Creator and Content Partnerships UK in an exclusive interview with Deadline. “Their roots in freestyle football, combined with humour, competition, personality and participation, resonate with what we’re seeing across audiences in the UK. Audiences aren’t bound by traditional genres; they are hungry for authentic storytelling from creators who speak to their interests and fuel their fandoms.” Qasem called Wheel of Misfortune “an important first step as Tubi’s first UK exclusive creator series” under the Tubi for Creators initiative. “We expect the UK slate to develop over time as we learn from audiences, creators and the performance of different formats,” he added. “Our strategy is to curate a slate of creator content on Tubi that feels distinct and puts fandom at the centre, with genuine audience connection. That’s what excites us at Tubi: not changing what makes creators distinctive, but giving them new ways to build out on it.” Tubi, which is part of Fox Corp, has been building out the Tubi for Creators program in line with global growth of the creator economy and its increasing impact on traditional TV players. The free streamer is available in 11 countries across North America, Latin America, Europe and Oceania, and Tubi is “exploring all opportunities” as “each market has its own creator ecosystem, cultural nuances and passionate fandoms,” said Qasem. ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Rides Into Awards Race; Mohsen Gharaei; Palestine Call Jeff Goldblum To Host S2 Premiere Of ‘Saturday Night Live UK’ Unifrance Rendez-Vous TV Preview & Interview Amid Industry Shifts Scroll Through Photos From Opening Day Of The 83rd Venice Film Festival Read More About: Comments

title: Sandra Hüller To Star As Celebrated Late Male German Artist Wolfgang Herrndorf’s In Maria Schrader’s ‘Work And Structure’
full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Sandra Hüller To Star As Celebrated Late Male German Artist Wolfgang Herrndorf’s In Maria Schrader’s ‘Work And Structure’ Calls Grow For Palestinian Flag To Fly At Venice Film Festival As Artistic Director Says Not Possible To Meet Request George Clooney Calls Out “Authoritarians” Who “Peddle Fear” As He Receives Lifetime Award Achievement In Venice View All September 3, 2026 3:06am Sandra Hüller Getty Images Oscar-nominated actress Sandra Hüller is set to star as late acclaimed German writer and artist Wolfgang Herrndorf in the upcoming feature Work and Structure ( Arbeit und Struktur ) by Maria Schrader . The production brings together two of Germany ‘s most celebrated female cinema professionals with Sandra Hüller seen this year in Paweł Pawlikowski’s Cannes winner Fatherland as well as opposite Ryan Gosling in Project Hail Mary , having previously won international acclaim for her performances in Anatomy of a Fall and The Zone of Interest . Schrader’s credits include the 2021 Berlinale selected She Said , I’m Your Man , for which star Maren Eggert won best acting performance, as well as Unorthodox and Stefan Zweig: Farewell to Europe . Watch on Deadline Related Stories News StudioCanal's 'Has Fallen' Series Returns For Season 3; Iwan Rheon, Brendan Coyle & Atandwa Kani Cast Festivals 'Krux' Trailer: Toronto-Bound WWII Drama Captures True Story Of Disintegration Of Order In German Village Herrndorf began documenting his life after being diagnosed with a terminal brain tumour in 2010. Published posthumously in 2013, the subsequent Work and Structure became a literary phenomenon in Germany and is now regarded as one of the defining works of contemporary German literature. Schrader, who is adapting the original work for the big screen with Jan Schomburg, said: “’Arbeit und Struktur’ is a solitary and intimate record of what it means to be alive. A man fights with words against his disappearance and, in the face of death, becomes more alive than ever before. Through his uncompromising honesty, his intelligence and irony, we follow Herrndorf into the bright, the dark and the secret corners of the human condition. Bringing that to the screen is one of the most exciting tasks I can imagine.” Hüller added of her involvement: “Ever since my first encounter with Wolfgang Herrndorf’s work, I have been unable to let go of his writing. His texts are at once surprising, unsettling, and comforting. To encounter him as a person through this film: at a moment when his life changed abruptly, seemed on the verge of falling apart, and when he was simultaneously discovering his voice as a writer before it was tragically silenced, is both a great honour and a profound challenge for me.” The synopsis for the planned film reads: “A powerful and deeply human story about creativity, friendship, love and mortality, Arbeit und Struktur follows an artist confronting the certainty of his own death with extraordinary honesty, wit and imagination. Through a profoundly personal journey, the film explores what remains when time becomes life’s most precious resource.” The feature is being produced by Komplizen Film, Studiocanal , Haut et Court and ZDF, with with production set to begin in early 2027. Studiocanal will handle world sales and release the film in Germany, France and Italy in 2028. The film is backed by Medienboard Berlin-Brandenburg, the Film- and Media Foundation NRW, the Federal Government’s jury-based cultural film funding programme, the German Federal Film Board FFA (Minitraité), and Creative Europe MEDIA Slate Development. ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Rides Into Awards Race; Mohsen Gharaei; Palestine Call Jeff Goldblum To Host S2 Premiere Of ‘Saturday Night Live UK’ Unifrance Rendez-Vous TV Preview & Interview Amid Industry Shifts Scroll Through Photos From Opening Day Of The 83rd Venice Film Festival Read More About: Comments

title: Unifrance’s Rendez-Vous Brings French Sellers & Global Buyers Together Amid Industry Shifts
full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart Unifrance’s Rendez-Vous Brings French Sellers & Global Buyers Together Amid Industry Shifts VodafoneThree Launching Vodafone TV In The UK, Bundling Netflix, HBO Max & Live Channels ‘Miraculous’ Studio Founder Jeremy Zag To Receive Deadline’s French TV Disruptor Award At The Unifrance Rendez-Vous View All September 3, 2026 2:34am Unifrance's Daniela Elstner, Le Havre, France. Marie Rouge/Martin Falbisoner The biggest French-language TV market of the year kicks off next week, marking its third year in the city of Le Havre in northern France. Organized by Unifrance, the org that promotes French TV and cinema, the annual Rendez-Vous has a different vibe to most markets. There’s a calendar of events meaning buyers and sellers eat, drink and attend a diary of events together, over and above screening shows and dealmaking through the day. Even though it’s a sizable event , the set-up gives the Rendez-Vous a unique feel. In an international TV biz that is changing fast, and with many events feeling the squeeze, creating that ambience is part of the plan, says Unifrance Executive Director Daniela Elstner . Related Stories News 'Miraculous' Studio Founder Jeremy Zag To Receive Deadline's French TV Disruptor Award At The Unifrance Rendez-Vous News French Star Patrick Bruel To Appear Before Investigating Judges As Sexual Misconduct Accusations Mount “The question is, how do you keep up with what people want from a market in a moment when things are shifting,” she says. “We have to somehow answer a lot of these questions. Maybe we don’t have all the answers, but what we can do is to create a moment where everyone is together. These are all people who love what they’re doing and are passionate, and we want to bring French programs to the world. Watch on Deadline “It is not only about what they are screening during the day, but it’s also about how we can be a place where everyone exchanges ideas and information and then discover new things.” Gathering In Le Havre Buyers and sellers network at a series of social events at the Rendez-Vous Unifrance, Jeremy-Charbaut, The main French distributors are in town, as usual. Buyer numbers are in line with last year, with about 135 expected in Le Havre. There’s an international spread, with acquisition execs mostly coming from Europe, but also first-time attendees from Brazil and South Korea are making the trip. Heavyweight European broadcasters including RAI, RTVE and ZDF will be there, as well as pay TV outfits including Sky Italia and HBO buyers covering central Europe. Having historically been in Saint Tropez and then Biarritz, Le Havre has hosted the Rendez-Vous for three years. Gaining support from the host city and region has helped the Rendez-Vous, which has a large sales floor, a theater for screenings and screening booths for buyers. The city and wider Normandy region have become embedded in proceedings, with the opening party held at the city’s Museum of Modern Art, and hosted by Édouard Philippe, Mayor of Le Havre. The closer is held at the historic Montivilliers Abbey and hosted by Hervé Morin, President of the Normandy Region. “The involvement of the city of Le Havre and also the region is like really great because this we didn’t experience it so much before [in previous locations],” Elstner says. Every Meeting Counts Bright Minds aka Astrid et Raphaëlle Patrick Fouque, FTV – JLA Support from the region helps, but the reality is buyers are attending fewer events and both programming and travel budgets are under pressure. Against that backdrop, market organizers must ensure any event offers buyers and sellers a clear return on investment. “They need to be reassured, and everything has to be very convenient and perfect in terms of organization, so that they can really concentrate on their meetings, what they are watching and the market,” says Elstner. The buyer-seller dynamic also shifts with fewer trips meaning fewer face-to-face meetings, she adds. “In previous times, you had many markets, so maybe a buyer having a meeting with a sales agent would be having one out of five such meetings with them in a year. But if it’s now just one out of two meetings a year, there is more pressure.” Industry Shifts The industry part of proceedings at Rendez-Vous traditionally sees the annual export stats for French-language programming revealed. This year there will be an additional layer of info presented with France’s National Cinema Centre, the CNC, providing the figures. In recent times the data has illustrated how France has become a big producer of cozy crime, with the likes of France TV Distribution’s Astrid et Raphaëlle , Gaumont’s L’Art Du Crime , Federation International’s Tropiques Criminels and TF1’s High Intellectual Potential leading the charge, the latter being remade as High Potential for U.S. network ABC. Animation, for so long a mainstay of the French biz, however, has been suffering. More broadly, linear channels in particular, are really feeling the pinch, with budgets and new slots declining. That’s a wider trend that will likely influence this year’s French TV export numbers. Irrespective of the challenges, the role of Unifrance is to bolster the international market for French shows, Elstner says. “We’re all facing more or less the same challenges worldwide. We can’t really help the programs themselves to be sold, but we can help our sales agents to be in a good shape and make their lives easier.” The Deadline French TV Disruptor Award will be presented to Jeremy Zag, founder of the studio behind French-originated global smash animated franchise Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir , which is a bright spot in terms of the French animation industry. The event, at the aforementioned Montivilliers Abbey, captures the spirit of the Rendez-Vous, with acquisition execs and sales folks mingling as local chefs showcase regional fare. Zag takes the Deadline honor, which was given to Fanny Herrero last year. “His career is really exceptional,” Elstner says. “It’s very interesting how from the very beginning he put a whole system in place, to not only create a series or film, but also a whole universe with great values.” The Unifrance Rendez-Vous runs from September 7 to 10 in Le Havre. ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Rides Into Awards Race; Mohsen Gharaei; Palestine Call Jeff Goldblum To Host S2 Premiere Of ‘Saturday Night Live UK’ Unifrance Rendez-Vous TV Preview & Interview Amid Industry Shifts Scroll Through Photos From Opening Day Of The 83rd Venice Film Festival Read More About: Comments
